newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt flat, but TCI reverses trend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt flat, but TCI reverses trend.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were mostly unchanged in thin trade on Monday, punctuated by a trend reversal for battered Tele-Communications Inc debt, high-grades traders said.
High-yielders tread water and closed with marginal weakness ahead of what some traders termed an ominous new issue calendar.
Back in the investment grades arena, traders said selling in Tele-Communications debt abated and spreads tightened for the first time in almost two weeks.

Traders said the reversal followed news that TCI's free cash flow will move into positive territory for the first time in several years and that capital spending is expected to fall to $1.6 billion in 1997 from an expected $2.0 billion in 1996. In addition, several traders said the debt was simply oversold after widening about 80 basis points in two weeks.
"It appears for the time being that some of the sellers are out of the market," one trader said, adding the widening has been driven much more by technicals than by fundamentals.
Myriad high-grades investors sold because of the threat of a downgrade to junk status, the trader said.
TCI 6-7/8 percent 10-year debt traded at a spread of 245 basis points on Monday compared to a quote of 255 basis points at the close on Friday, one trader said.

Elsewhere, high-grade corporate issues were firm and quiet ahead of a host of economic data through next week and the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding. Data this week includes employment cost data on Tuesday, third quarter GDP on Wednesday and October jobs data and the NAPM survey on Friday.
Treasury prices were slightly defensive in anticipation of data, analysts said, and the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 9/32 to 98-28/32 to yield 6.84 percent.
Turning to high-yielders, prices wavered in response to a mounting new issue calendar and suddenly lackluster mutual fund cash flows, dealers said.
"The market feels heavy and that's with a load of things to look at in November," one high-yield trader said, adding that typically dull Monday activity also jaded sentiment.

Some of the bigger movers on Monday included Sinclair Broadcasting debt, which dropped about three points after a disappointing earnings report, a trader said. Sinclair's shares fell 4-3/4 points to 29-1/4 on Monday.
UniLab debt fell five points on Monday morning on Street expectations of weak earnings, one trader said.

New issuance was topped by Mexican bottler Coca-Cola FEMSA's $200 million 10-year 8.95 percent B1/B-plus rated notes, priced via J.P. Morgan Securities Inc to yield 8.956 percent or 240 basis points over the Treasury curve.
John Massad, head of syndicate at J.P. Morgan, said the issue was priced below initial price talk and was more than two times oversubscribed.
The offering was increased in size by $25 million.
